name: DTH-PHC overlay on the DPI-H reference architecture
documentation: Overlay of dth-phc on smart-ra ArchiMate 0.3.0-draft.1. Elements tagged overlay:base are reference copies of smart-ra elements (the IRI names the original); elements tagged overlay:owner=dth-phc are added by this DTH and are not part of smart-ra. Built by scripts/archimate/extract_overlay.py.

elements.name: Implementing team
elements.documentation: Multidisciplinary project and implementation team commissioning and coordinating requirements gathering, software and vendor selection, design and adaptation, end-user training, user acceptance testing, deployment, and scale-up in collaboration with the public health authority and technology partners. (Section 2.2, Ch. 3-6 panels, PDF 24, 30, 52, 64, 68)

properties.value: Digital health implementation team; Project team
WHO Digital Transformation Handbooks (PHC 9789240093362, SC 9789240116214, PC 9789240116191, HRH, SFP); litlfred/smart-ra#133

elements.name: Public health authority
elements.documentation: National or subnational public health authority (such as a ministry of health) responsible for governance, health and digital health policies, change management, local adoption, cybersecurity, privacy, confidentiality, data use policies, and leading scale-up and phase-out of paper or legacy systems. (Section 2.2, Ch. 3, 5 & 6 panels, PDF 24, 30, 64, 68)

properties.value: Ministry of health; Subnational health authority
WHO Digital Transformation Handbooks (PHC 9789240093362, SC 9789240116214, PC 9789240116191, HRH, SFP); litlfred/smart-ra#133

elements.name: Business analyst
elements.documentation: Gathers and optimizes the content and functional requirements for adapting or developing a digital health solution; leads requirements gathering alongside health informaticians and user researchers, and provides continuous feedback to the engineering team during design and adaptation to ensure proper translation of requirements into implementation. (Section 2.2, Ch. 3-4 panels, PDF 24, 30, 52)

properties.value: WHO Digital Transformation Handbooks (PHC 9789240093362, SC 9789240116214, PC 9789240116191, HRH, SFP); litlfred/smart-ra#133

elements.name: Designer
elements.documentation: Develops and tests prototype designs (mock-ups, wireframes, interactive prototypes) and provides continuous feedback with business analysts to the engineering team to translate user requirements into user interface design. (Section 2.2, Ch. 4 panel, Section 4.3, PDF 24, 52, 54-55)

properties.value: UX/UI designer; Service designer; Software designer
WHO Digital Transformation Handbooks (PHC 9789240093362, SC 9789240116214, PC 9789240116191, HRH, SFP); litlfred/smart-ra#133

elements.name: Health informatician
elements.documentation: Leads requirements gathering alongside business analysts and user researchers, and provides expert guidance during design and adaptation to ensure the digital health system adheres to semantic classifications, terminology standards and syntactic interoperability standards such as HL7 FHIR. (Section 2.2, Ch. 3-4 panels, PDF 24, 30, 52)

properties.value: WHO Digital Transformation Handbooks (PHC 9789240093362, SC 9789240116214, PC 9789240116191, HRH, SFP); litlfred/smart-ra#133

elements.name: Health service user
elements.documentation: Also known as patients, clients or beneficiaries, these are individuals who receive formal and/or informal health services. (PDF 9, 18)

properties.value: Health service users; Patient; Client; Beneficiary
WHO Digital transformation handbook for primary health care: optimizing person-centred point of service systems (9789240093362); litlfred/dth-phc

elements.name: Health worker
elements.documentation: End-users of a PCPOSS at the point of care (point of service), including all health worker occupational groups operating at all care levels and outside of formal health-care facilities (e.g. community health workers and health volunteers). (PDF 19)

properties.value: WHO Digital transformation handbook for primary health care: optimizing person-centred point of service systems (9789240093362); litlfred/dth-phc

elements.name: Monitoring and evaluation specialist
elements.documentation: Determines whether the digital health system meets required performance metrics and benchmarks during scale-up so that the public health authority can safely phase out paper and/or legacy systems. (Ch. 6 panel, Section 6.3, PDF 68, 70)

properties.value: WHO Digital Transformation Handbooks (PHC 9789240093362, SC 9789240116214, PC 9789240116191, HRH, SFP); litlfred/smart-ra#133

elements.name: Software engineer
elements.documentation: Engaged during requirements gathering to understand the operational context, leads solution design, adaptation, build and quality assurance alongside solutions architects, and incorporates end-user feedback during training, testing and roll-out. (Ch. 3-5 panels, PDF 30, 52, 64)

properties.value: WHO Digital Transformation Handbooks (PHC 9789240093362, SC 9789240116214, PC 9789240116191, HRH, SFP); litlfred/smart-ra#133

elements.name: Solutions architect
elements.documentation: Leads system architecture design and adaptation alongside software engineers, defining how software components, data services and interoperability standards fit within the national digital health enterprise architecture. (Ch. 4 panel, Section 4.4, PDF 52, 56-60)

properties.value: WHO Digital Transformation Handbooks (PHC 9789240093362, SC 9789240116214, PC 9789240116191, HRH, SFP); litlfred/smart-ra#133

elements.name: Technology partner
elements.documentation: Software vendor or technology partner selected to build, adapt, maintain and update the digital health solution across design, adaptation, deployment and scale-up phases in collaboration with the implementing team. (Section 2.2, Ch. 4 & 6 panels, Section 4.1, PDF 24, 52-53, 68)

properties.value: WHO Digital Transformation Handbooks (PHC 9789240093362, SC 9789240116214, PC 9789240116191, HRH, SFP); litlfred/smart-ra#133

elements.name: User researcher
elements.documentation: Person trained in user research who leads the process of understanding end-users, conducting contextual observations and interviews, and gathering user requirements alongside business analysts and health informaticians. (Ch. 3 panel, Sections 3.1-3.2, PDF 30-35)

elements.name: Community-based information system
elements.documentation: Applications that facilitate data collection and use at the community level. These applications are utilized by community-based workers who provide health promotion and disease prevention activities. (PDF 8, 18)

properties.value: WHO Digital transformation handbook for primary health care: optimizing person-centred point of service systems (9789240093362); litlfred/dth-phc

elements.name: Decision support system
elements.documentation: A digital job aid that combines an individual's health information with the health worker's knowledge and clinical protocols, to assist health workers in making diagnosis and treatment decisions. (PDF 8, 18)

properties.value: WHO Digital transformation handbook for primary health care: optimizing person-centred point of service systems (9789240093362); litlfred/dth-phc

elements.name: Electronic health record system
elements.documentation: A secure, online system that holds health service user health records, which include information about people's health and clinical care. This system is managed by health workers. Also referred to as an 'electronic medical record system'. (PDF 8, 18)

properties.value: WHO Digital transformation handbook for primary health care: optimizing person-centred point of service systems (9789240093362); litlfred/dth-phc

elements.name: Personal health record
elements.documentation: A record of an individual's health information in a structured digital format for a set of defined use cases over which the person has agency. (PDF 18)

properties.value: WHO Digital transformation handbook for primary health care: optimizing person-centred point of service systems (9789240093362); litlfred/dth-phc

elements.name: Point-of-service application
elements.documentation: Person-centred point of service system (PCPOSS) are digital systems that facilitate the provision and delivery of health services to individuals (i.e. persons, clients, patients, health service users) at the point of service or point of care. This includes software capabilities and embedded health interoperability standards that enable health workers to access, record and update individuals' health information, and to screen, manage, treat, and/or communicate with individuals. PCPOSS encompass community-based information systems, decision support systems, electronic health record systems and personal health records. (PDF 9, 18)

properties.value: WHO Digital transformation handbook for primary health care: optimizing person-centred point of service systems (9789240093362); litlfred/dth-phc

elements.name: Alerts and reminders
elements.documentation: DHI 1.1.3 Transmit targeted alerts and reminders to health service user(s); DHI 2.3.1 Provide prompts and alerts according to protocols. (PDF 18)

elements.name: Care checklists

elements.name: Clinical screening
elements.documentation: DHI 2.3.3 Screen persons by risk or other health status; DHI 2.7.1 Identify persons in need of services. (PDF 18)

properties.value: WHO Digital transformation handbook for primary health care: optimizing person-centred point of service systems (9789240093362); litlfred/dth-phc

elements.name: Indicator reporting
elements.documentation: DHI 2.2.4 Routine health indicator data collection and management; DHI 4.1.2 Data storage and aggregation; DHI 4.1.3 Data synthesis and visualizations. Collect primary data once at the point of care to calculate aggregate indicators for reporting and accountability (Fig. 4, PDF 18-19).

elements.name: Longitudinal tracking
elements.documentation: DHI 2.2.1 Longitudinal tracking of a health service user's health status and services: ongoing and systematic collection and analysis of data related to a health service user's health status, treatment and outcomes over multiple encounters or visits. (PDF 9, 18)

views.name: Person-centred point of service (PCPOSS)
views.documentation: Person-centred point of service system (PCPOSS) and its four specialized application types (electronic health record system, decision support system, community-based information system, personal health record), the five PCPOSS digital health intervention services (Section 1.1, PDF 18), end-user roles (Health worker and Health service user / Patients), and interoperability with foundational DPI-H registries, repositories, terminology, clinical decision support and analytics (Fig. 4, Section 4.4, PDF 18-19, 56-60).

views.name: Shared DTH Roles and Actors
views.documentation: Shared Digital Transformation Handbook (DTH) governance, implementation, specialist and end-user roles and actors (smart-ra#133 comment 1; dth-phc#1 §3d / Step P5), linking the Implementing team, Public health authority, Technology partner and specialist Business Roles (Business analyst, Health informatician, User researcher, Designer, Solutions architect, Software engineer, Monitoring and evaluation specialist, National Regulatory Authority) with end-user roles (Health worker, Health service user) and 0.2.0 Stakeholders (Ministry of Health, Health Workers, Patients).
